cases.note: The field names one object in blob storage, and `under` names the place the row's own bytes live in: {ownerUserId} is the field the concept's @rowAuthz(owner=...) names, which the write guard holds to the writer's own user id. An account export copies the object only when its key lies strictly inside that place.

`tree`: the field names a prefix, and the bytes are every object under it; {id} is the row's own id. `counted`: the bytes are counted in the file's report and never carried. Either takes a list of strings as well as a string, and both still name their place.
A counted field's bytes are sized in an export's report and never read, so its place may be literal: an attachment's key is built from values that are not fields of the row.
A counted field may name any top-level string field, since nothing is read from the place it builds.
